children: Brunello Cucinelli looks favorably disconnected from the wider luxury-fashion sector, Bernstein says. The Italian fashion house, known for its cashmere, bucked weak trends elsewhere in luxury with a 13.5% rise in third-quarter sales, lifting its 2026 expectations on the back of that impetus. "The disconnect with the sector is felt particularly when looking at growth by geography, which was driven by the Americas and China where they are welcoming new customers to the brand," Bernstein notes. (joshua.kirby@wsj.com; @joshualeokirby)
